theAnswer.question: If I were handed this corpus and told to build the v1 slice, would I succeed?
theAnswer.verdict: NO — but the reasons are not the ones the corpus tells me they are.
theAnswer.inOneParagraph: I can build most of the spine to a genuinely high standard: I resolved the C-2 derivation chain, reproduced 7/7 planIntentCommitment vectors, 5/5 PLAN-ID-V1 vectors, 3/3 SNAPSHOT-ID-V1, 2/2 FACT-ID-V1, 7/7 CAP-MANIFEST-ID-V1 and 17/17 POLICY-DERIVATION-DIGEST-V1 vectors, each from published prose, with code sharing nothing with any corpus checker. The D9 oracle imports and reproduces 45/45 goldens. The Rust wire protocol's framing, CBOR, limits, commitments and 28-rule state machine are all determinable. That is a lot of working architecture. But the v1 slice cannot be COMPLETED, and separately I cannot START week one obediently, because the two instructions the blueprint gives me most emphatically at §7.2 steps 3 and 5 are both wrong — the rules they say do not exist were added to their owning surfaces' heads on 2026-08-05 and I reproduced both. The document set has not caught up with its own applications.
theAnswer.theShapeOfTheFailure: The corpus is not under-specified where it says it is. It is under-specified somewhere else, and it is over-cautious where it has already succeeded. Three of the four things I am told to escalate in week one are closed; four things I am NOT told about are genuinely uncomputable and stop the milestone.
theAnswer.wouldIHaveGuessed: Yes, twice, and both guesses would have been defensible and both are forbidden. (1) At §7.2 step 3 I would have shipped the CAP-MANIFEST-ID-V1 recipe I found in the applied DELIVERY head rather than stalling, because §1.1 rule 2 says the artifact's CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED self-declaration is not a verdict. (2) At §7.2 step 5 I would have done the same for POLICY-DERIVATION-DIGEST-V1. Under freeze §7.1 — 'None may be closed by ... an implementer' — both are inventions. That is why they are findings and not decisions.

findings.severityJustification: Two clauses of one section give different byte orderings for the same map. The specific clause governs and it is implementable — but the label is a trap for anyone who reaches for an off-the-shelf RFC 8949 deterministic encoder, which is the obvious thing to do.

findings.measurement: RFC 8949 §4.2.1 core deterministic encoding is bytewise-lexicographic map ordering. Length-first is §4.2.3, the OLD RFC 7049 canonical ordering. The two agree on equal-length keys and disagree on unequal-length keys. Every mainstream Rust CBOR crate implements §4.2.1 when asked for 'deterministic'.
findings.whatIWouldDo: Implement length-first per `mapOrder` and NOT use a library's deterministic mode. I would flag it, because a reviewer reading `standard:` will believe the opposite.
findings.whatIWouldNeedToProceed: Correct the `standard` label to name RFC 8949 §4.2.3 / RFC 7049 canonical, or change `mapOrder`.

Neither grammar is declared, and a resolver written for one crashes on the other. Additionally three `planIntentFixtures` keys contain literal dots (`analysis.work-units`, `analysis.bytes`, `analysis.milliseconds`) and the dotted grammar has no escape — harmless today only because no operation addresses them.

items: **Every pin holds.** All 23 §1.1-pinned artifacts and checkers recompute to their published SHA-256, plus `v1-slice.md` at `6b8717fe…` and `ARCHITECTURE-TO-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` at `47df412d…`. Zero drift. Every checker and every review artifact named in §1.1 exists on disk. The version-selection defect that failed the first litmus is genuinely repaired.

**The derivation instruction works.** The blueprint told me to resolve a chain rather than read a file, and I did: C-2 at depth 3 (39 operations, 3 predecessor digests verified, 0 from-mismatches, 0 resolve errors), DELIVERY at depth 1 (21 operations, 7 `from` matches, 0 refusals), TM storageNamespace at depth 1 (13 operations). All three produced usable contracts. The `from` precondition on every `set` is the single best design choice in the format — it makes a misapplied derivation impossible rather than merely detectable.

**Six identity recipes reproduce from published prose, first attempt, with code sharing nothing with any corpus checker.** `planIntentCommitment` 7/7. `SNAPSHOT-ID-V1` 3/3. `PLAN-ID-V1` 5/5 including both positive goldens at their declared preimage byte lengths (2500 and 8208), both transformations and the EPC-V1 separating vector. `FACT-ID-V1` 2/2 including intermediate CBOR hex. `CAP-MANIFEST-ID-V1` 7/7 with literal `decode(encode(x)) == x` on all 7. `POLICY-DERIVATION-DIGEST-V1` 17/17 across five independent checks each. That is a high bar and these bytes clear it.

**The D9 oracle instruction works and the oracle is real.** Import under `python3 -I` takes 0.066s from any working directory; `derive_class` reproduces 45/45 goldens; `reduce_concurrent` reproduces 5/5; the pin verification is enforced at module exec, so tampering a scratch copy raises `PinMismatch` before any export is usable. All five documented signature strings match `inspect.signature` character-for-character, and `NPA-5` re-derives them from the contract every run — which is genuinely self-enforcing, just not for semantics (IL4-01).

**R-1 v1.6 is the best-specified surface for a Rust port I have seen in an architecture corpus.** It hands over the exact `evaluate` signature, borrow discipline, output ownership, a `noLifetimeFork` rule and a 9-member `forbiddenPublicShapes` list naming the specific Rust anti-patterns it forbids. 25 closed types with fieldOrder, `optionalFields`, `additionalProperties: false`, and an orderRule plus uniquenessRule on every collection. `CoreDeps` carries a 20-member `forbiddenFields` list that encodes the whole purity argument as data.

**The Rust wire protocol is buildable and the two v2 blockers are genuinely discharged.** I checked the discharge-by-deletion rather than accepting it: the one live reference to a deleted selector dies with its own replaced parent. Framing (40 prefix bytes, reject-before-allocate), 24 uint64 limits with a byte-equality handshake, 9 domain-separated commitment formulas, 21 frame types, and a 28-rule state machine with an explicit totality table and a named catch-all — all determinable.

**FACT-PLANE's closed enumerations are complete and rank-free, which is the C-1 argument made structural rather than argued.** 12 relations, 12 payload schemas, 5 layers explicitly rank-free, 5 deficiencies ordered by remedy specificity, per-relation ladders that are total (8 one-rung, 4 two-rung) with no global order, and 4 explicitly FORBIDDEN envelope fields (`quality`, `tier`, `degraded`, `rank`). Freeze §6 law 3's 'why may I not just degrade to the syntactic answer' is answered by the type system, not by a paragraph.

**Every SEAL-WITH-CHANGES adjudication's required changes were applied in place.** I checked all three (fact-plane R1-FP-01/02/03, resolved-inputs R1-RI-01/02/03, fact-identity R2-FI-01..06) and found no unapplied-change trap and no missing successor version. The sealed bytes and the buildable bytes are the same bytes.

**The layer-4 contradiction is handled the way a corpus should handle a contradiction.** `v1-slice.md` §6 says CI must 'ignore layer 4 entirely OR fail admission' with the choice still open; the binding packet says `CI_IGNORES_LAYER_4` and 'their presence is not an admission failure'. §2's authority order already decides it, freeze §5.1 RECORDS the disagreement rather than editing the pinned file, and `check-narrative-packet-agreement.py` re-derives the disagreement set from live bytes every run and hard-compares it in BOTH directions. It exits 0 at 3 derived = 3 recorded. Freeze §8 lists 'choose layer-4 CI behavior' as a package-failure condition and I was never made to choose.

**Instrument self-reports reproduce exactly.** `check-completeness.py`: shape 11/13, reviewed 13/13, seal-ready 9/13, 1 cross-cutting open (`R2-FINAL-03`), exit 1 — every figure as published. `check-threat-claims.py`: exactly the 2 documented `T1` findings, both against narrative and neither against the JSON. `check-claims.py`: 33 claims, 27/27 homes, 32/32 restatements, CHK-0..CHK-5 clean. The blueprint's warning that `check-versioning-v8.py` is now red and freeze §9.1's claim is stale: both confirmed.

**The `rg` trap is documented with unusual precision and it is exactly right.** `command -v rg` succeeds on this host (shell function) while `shutil.which("rg")` returns `None`, and the checker fails with `FileNotFoundError` before any contract property is evaluated. The blueprint's insistence that this exit 1 is 'not a finding' and that one must 'assert on finding identity, never on the exit code' is correct and I would have mis-recorded it otherwise.

**The §7.1 park stated as a PROPERTY rather than a list did its job.** IL4-12 (`FindingValue.valueDigest`) and three of the five tag-9 digests in IL4-13 are in no row, no sweep and no package document, and the property made escalating them compliant with no amendment. The corpus's own conclusion — 'an enumeration of named items goes stale silently in both directions, while the limb stated as a property covered the case correctly without being edited either time' — is validated by this run. It is also, precisely, why IL4-02/03/05/06/07 exist: the ROWS went stale in the other direction and nothing re-derives them.

**Nothing in this run forced a §8 package-failure choice.** I was not made to choose retention, invent a second store authority, decide the core effect boundary, select a Rust substrate, choose layer-4 CI behaviour, create an exit mapping, or decide which version of a binding artifact is normative. On the last one, §1.1 answered every time I asked.

closingStatement: The architecture in this corpus is good. The identity work is better than good — six recipes reproduced first-try from prose by independent code is a standard most specifications never reach, and R-1 v1.6 and the RUST-PROVIDER-PROTOCOL state machine are documents I would be glad to implement against. What stops me is not architecture. Four values genuinely do not exist (`FindingValue.valueDigest`, `RunId`, the sealed-Run manifest identity, `EvidenceDigest`), one specification genuinely does not exist (FACT-IDENTITY's canonical level specification), the substrate is unpinned, and Phase-1A has not landed. Those are six real walls and they are worth the wait. What is NOT worth anything is the seventh wall: the corpus telling me, in five places, to stop on work its own applied heads completed on 2026-08-05. That one costs a week and buys nothing, and it is fixed by editing text that already exists.
